newsitem.title: FRANCE: Protesters demand trial for Zaire envoy to France.
newsitem.headline: Protesters demand trial for Zaire envoy to France.

text.p: Some 400 protesters gathered on Friday at a Riviera pedestrian crossing where the car of Zaire's envoy to France fatally hit two boys last month, demanding that the diplomat be brought to trial.

The protesters said they would gather outside the villa of Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko in nearby Roquebrune-Cap-Martin on February 1 unless he lifted Ambassador Ramazani Baya's diplomatic immunity.

"This is a struggle of ordinary people against those who always enjoy privileges," said Bernard Bourie, the head of the local schoolchildren's parents association as the protesters lit symbolical candles to demand that light be shed on the accident.
France has vowed to bring Baya to justice after he drove over the pedestrian crossing at more than twice the legal speed limit, hitting the teenagers.

Baya, who is believed to be in Zaire, has offered to forfeit his diplomatic immunity shielding him from trial in France. But Kinshasa has said he could not renounce it and only the Zaire government could lift it.
Thierry Giorgio, a lawyer for the family of one of the boys, called on Paris to take sanctions against Zaire.
The accident occurred as the envoy hurried to visit Mobutu who was resting at his villa from prostate cancer treatment in Switzerland.
Mobutu flew to Zaire last month and returned to his French Riviera villa earlier this month. Zaire officials said he had consulted French doctors and would soon return to Kinshasa.
